evals.prompt: A feature on one instance does nothing. Its config references the key it needs and the reference looks correct. Nothing appears in the log. What is wrong?
evals.expected_output: The config states what is required; only the injection wrapper states what is delivered. Compare the two sets by name — a required key that is not delivered kills the feature silently.
expectations: Distinguishes required (config references) from delivered (wrapper output)
Compares the two sets by key name, never by value
Treats a non-empty required-minus-delivered set as critical
Does not conclude the key is missing from a bare exec that bypasses the wrapper

evals.prompt: Every key in this instance's plaintext env file is also in the secret store, so delete the file and restart.
evals.expected_output: Refuses until fingerprint parity is proven key by key. A single key the store does not deliver makes the file load-bearing, and deleting it kills the instance at the next restart. Neutralisation is a move to quarantine outside every container volume, not a delete.
expectations: Classifies the file by per-key fingerprint parity, not by the file existing
Closes the gap for load-bearing keys before moving anything
Moves the file to quarantine outside container volumes instead of deleting it
Restarts one canary instance and verifies before rolling the rest

evals.prompt: Here is the new API key: put it in the store for all instances.
evals.expected_output: The plugin does not accept a key in chat — the value is now in the transcript and on disk. It prints a line that reads the value with echo disabled, pipes it to the write, and discards both output streams; verification is by fingerprint.
expectations: Refuses to take the value through the conversation and says why
Prints an operator line reading the value with echo off, value never in argv
Discards both output streams because the write prints a full key-value table even when quiet
Verifies by fingerprint and key name only
Treats the pasted value as leaked and calls for rotation

evals.prompt: Restart all the managed instances so they pick up the config change.
evals.expected_output: Restart is reversible but carries an irreversible precondition here: a running instance holds its secrets in memory and a restart re-resolves them. Run the delivery audit first and refuse while any required key is undelivered.
expectations: Runs the delivery audit before the restart, not after
Shows the resolved key names in the precheck block
Refuses while required-minus-delivered is non-empty
Goes canary first rather than restarting the whole fleet at once

evals.prompt: The identity token works when I run the login by hand, but the same command in my script produces a token every later call rejects.
evals.expected_output: The store CLI writes its update-check banner to stderr. A capture that merges the streams glues the banner onto the token. Capture stdout alone.
expectations: Identifies the merged stderr banner as the cause
Says to capture stdout only
Notes the resulting error misleadingly blames the credentials

evals.prompt: A backup file on the box contained a gateway token in plaintext. I deleted the backup, so we are clear.
evals.expected_output: No: deletion removes the evidence, not the exposure. If the value ever left the box, rotation is mandatory — new value written, instances rolled canary first, and the old value invalidated at the provider.
expectations: States that deleting the file does not undo the compromise
Requires rotation rather than recommending it
Includes invalidating the old value at the provider as part of the rotation
Does not let the completed easy action stand in for the undone one

evals.prompt: One instance gets three keys from the store while its siblings each get around fourteen. Is the store down?
evals.expected_output: No — the store is fine for the siblings. A fraction of the expected key set points at a wrong project or environment binding on that instance's identity; almost none points at a broken identity.
expectations: Compares the delivered count against the siblings and the configured expected count
Separates a wrong project or environment binding from a broken identity by how many keys arrive
Checks the identity file presence, ownership and mode
Compares key names, not just counts
